title: RIIC Office AI Operating System
client: RIIC, a university research and innovation office
metaDescription: An AI operating system for RIIC, a university research and innovation office, built on Nod. It runs on the office laptop and handles email, briefings, minutes, memos and calendar, with the team approving anything that goes out.
hook: The office now has one AI system, on its own laptop, that does the work and never acts without the team.

card.challenge: Email, meetings, memos, minutes and follow-up were all done by hand, across different tools, and the data could not leave the office.
card.actions: Built it on Nod as a local harness on the office laptop, with its own skills and tools, a main brain, a backup brain, and a team approval step before anything goes out.
card.results: It runs the office as one operation: email sorted into 8 categories, briefings, minutes, memos, calendar and reminders, with a log of who did what.

challenge: The office had no single system for its work. Email, meetings, memos, minutes, graphics and follow-up were all happening by hand, across different tools, and that data could not leave the office.
actions: I built the office AI operating system on Nod, with a local harness that runs on the office's own laptop, and turned the separate workflows into a single operation. It has its own skills, capabilities and tools, a main brain, and a backup brain: if the first model fails, the work moves to the backup. Because it runs locally, the office controls its data. Nothing goes to external parties, and the data is not used to train models or exposed.

It never sends or does anything without the team's approval. That human check is what makes it a solid agentic loop: the system can draft, log, remind and prepare the work, but the team gives permission before anything goes out.

It has its own main folder on Google Drive, and that folder holds the context that grounds the AI. An activity log with tabs for project management and work management records every task, who did it, and whether it is completed, pending or rejected. It logs urgent emails, drafts replies and sends those drafts to the team, then updates the log when the team takes action. It runs the office email: it classifies and labels every incoming message into 8 categories, messages me on anything urgent, and keeps the inbox organised.

It sends a morning briefing and an end-of-day briefing, and logs both. Meeting minutes go into a minutes folder. It has calendar access: it saves events, knows the office members' emails, adds them as invitees, and can create, edit or delete events, including Google Meet links. Memos are saved and tracked in a memo folder. It can make graphics in the school colours in Canva, and it reminds the team of work already done and what is still pending.
results: The system is running in the RIIC office as one operation, on the office laptop. Email, briefings, minutes, memos, calendar and follow-up now sit in one place, with a log of who did what.
If the main model fails, the backup takes over. Nothing goes out unless the team approves it, and the office keeps control of its data.

homeLine: An AI system that runs a research office's inbox, minutes and calendar, with the team approving every move.

title: RIIC Certificate System
client: RIIC, a university research and innovation office
metaDescription: One n8n certificate workflow, used for a capacity-building workshop and an international conference, that sent a personalised certificate and message to over 400 participants, with a Google Apps Script verification layer.
hook: One workflow, two events, a personalised certificate for every participant.

card.challenge: Two events needed a named certificate and message for every participant, and the conference registration link had spread across WhatsApp groups.
card.actions: Built one n8n workflow that fills the certificate, saves it to Drive and emails it, plus an Apps Script check that issued 8-character access codes and sorted every entry as valid, duplicate or invalid.
card.results: Used for over 400 participants across both events. Duplicate and invalid submissions were stopped before the certificate run.

challenge: For both the September capacity-building workshop and the ICTR-LD 2026 conference, the office needed to get a personalised certificate and message to every participant. Doing that by hand meant typing names into a template, exporting PDFs and emailing people one by one.
For the conference, a shared registration link also spread across WhatsApp groups, so the list itself had to be protected.
actions: I built one certificate workflow and used it for both events. The Canva certificate template goes into Google Slides. n8n reads each name from a sheet, fills the certificate, saves the file to Drive, and emails the participant a personalised message with their certificate.

For ICTR-LD, I added a Google Apps Script verification layer across 5 Google services (Sheets, Forms, Slides, Drive, Gmail). It issued unique 8-character access codes to 2 participant groups, emailed each person a prefilled personal link, and sorted every submission into 3 states: valid, duplicate, or invalid. Only verified names went into the certificate run.
The workflow has its own error workflow, and it was built to be safe to repeat: it skipped anyone already sent.
results: The same system was used for both events. Each participant received a personalised message and their certificate. It was used for over 400 people.
Duplicate and invalid conference submissions were stopped before they reached the certificate list.

title: Event Registration and Ticketing System
client: Babcock PPA Corpers Hangout, a social event
metaDescription: A paid registration and ticketing system for a social event: Lovable landing page and form, n8n webhooks, Google Drive, Airtable and a personalised day-of message. Over 45 people registered.
hook: Paid registration for a social event, from receipt upload to a personal message on the day.

card.challenge: The hangout needed paid registration and proof of payment, without chasing receipts or writing to people one by one.
card.actions: Built a Lovable landing page and form. An n8n webhook saved each receipt to Drive, logged the entry in Airtable and sent a pending email, with separate workflows for approval and errors.
card.results: Over 45 people registered, and on the day each one got a personalised message with the venue and time.

challenge: The hangout needed paid registration, proof of payment, and a way to keep the list and the messages in order. Doing that by hand would have meant chasing receipts, typing names into a sheet, and writing to people one by one.
actions: I built a Lovable landing page and a registration form (email, full name, WhatsApp number, receipt upload). An n8n webhook received each submission, saved the receipt to Google Drive, logged a pending record in Airtable, and sent a registration-pending email.

Separate published workflows handled ticket approval and errors, including its own error workflow. On the day, each registered person got a personalised message with their name, the venue and the 2:00 PM time.
results: The registration system went live and was used for the hangout. Over 45 people registered.
Receipts landed in Drive, registrations landed in Airtable with verification status and ticket price, and people received a personalised day-of message.
